title: Opportunity Clicks—FedEx Keeps E-Commerce Moving for the Holidays
summary: FedEx outlines its solutions for e-retailers during the critical holiday shopping season, emphasizing speed, reliability, and cost-saving options for shipping and returns. The article provides tips for online businesses to remain competitive in a "free shipping world" and highlights various FedEx services that simplify logistics and enhance customer satisfaction. It also details easy return solutions for businesses of all sizes, including integration with USPS for higher-volume returns.

title: Why Netflix is Broken and How to Fix it
summary: Netflix is facing significant challenges, including subscriber loss due to price increases, rising streaming content costs, and tough competition. An analyst suggests that Netflix's pricing strategy alienated hybrid customers and that across-the-board price increases and tempered international expansion would have been more effective. Netflix is expected to face continued losses in 2012 partly due to its international expansion efforts.

title: Package Volumes Projected to Spike on December 12 as FedEx Hits its Busiest Day in History
summary: FedEx announced that December 12, 2011, was projected to be its busiest day in company history, with an estimated 17 million shipments. To manage this surge, FedEx added 20,000 seasonal positions and increased shifts for existing team members. The company highlighted its technological precision and network flexibility in handling the growing holiday shipping volumes.

title: You Press the Button. Kodak Used to Do the Rest.
summary: This article examines why Kodak, despite anticipating the shift to digital photography and even pioneering some digital technologies, ultimately failed to adapt and thrive in the new market. It highlights Kodak's core business being film processing ("doing the rest"), which became obsolete with digital imaging, and how its former competitive advantages turned into liabilities. The piece argues that the company's vertically integrated film business model could not successfully transition to the low-margin digital camera market.

title: Princeton, NJ – Amazon CEO Bezos Donate $15M To Princeton
summary: Amazon.com Inc. founder and CEO Jeff Bezos and his wife, MacKenzie Bezos, have donated $15 million to Princeton University, their alma mater. The donation will establish the Bezos Center for Neural Circuit Dynamics within the Princeton Neuroscience Institute. This new center will focus on understanding the brain, investigating neurological disorders, and studying how brain operations affect behavior and learning.

title: UPS, FedEx holiday package volume up from 2010
summary: UPS and FedEx are experiencing significantly increased package volumes during the 2011 holiday season compared to the previous year, driven by a surge in online sales. UPS expects to deliver over 120 million parcels globally in the peak week, a 6% increase, while FedEx saw a 10% jump in its busiest day's volume. Both companies have hired thousands of seasonal workers and additional jets to manage the rush, reflecting a positive indicator for the broader economy.

title: International Amazon.com Best-Selling Books of 2011 By Business Wire Dec 24, 2011 - 3:19:40 PM
summary: Amazon.com released its top 10 best-selling books of 2011, with "Steve Jobs" by Walter Isaacson taking the number one spot. Notably, "The Mill River Recluse" and "The Abbey," independently published through Kindle Direct Publishing, secured positions on the list based solely on Kindle sales without a print edition. This highlights the growing influence of self-published digital content in the book market.
